title: The bacterial growth curve
caption: Plotted as log₁₀ of the number of living cells, exponential growth is a straight line: with a 20-minute generation time the count doubles three times an hour (log₁₀ 2 = 0.301 per generation). A lag phase comes first, then the log phase, a stationary phase when growth equals death, and a death phase.
alt: A curve of log of viable cell count against time in hours: flat for the first hour (lag), a straight rising line from 1 to 6 hours (log phase), flat from 6 to 10 hours (stationary) and falling afterwards (death).
description: Lag phase, the first hour: the cells adjust and make enzymes, with little division.
Log phase: the count doubles every generation (20 minutes here), a straight line on a log scale: gradient 0.903 per hour.
Stationary phase: growth equals death as nutrients run out and wastes build up.
Death phase: more cells die than divide.
After n generations the population is the starting number × 2ⁿ: ten generations multiply it 1,024-fold.
axisLabels: log₁₀ of living cells per mL

checks.name: lag phase: no change in the count
